r0.why: Smallest Galilean moon, binoculars, rock, possible Fe-Ni core, thin O2 atmosphere, closest icy Galilean per [1,2,3,5,6].

r1.why: Tan cracks, no mountains/craters, smoothest, young surface shaped by tidal heating from close orbit per [3,4,7].

r2.why: Subsurface ocean explains young surface, possible life, tidal flexing model, sea salt and habitability per [8-11].

r3.why: Hubble plumes like Enceladus, May 2018 Galileo reanalysis, search without landing, March 2024 oxygen per [12-15].

r4.why: 8 Jan 1610 discovery, Marius independently, 7 Jan unresolved at Padua, naming myth, names revived mid-20th c., Jupiter II per cited.

r5.why: 3.55 days, 670,900 km, e=0.009, small inclination, tidal lock, sub-Jovian point, non-synchronous rotation per [40-45].

r6.why: Flybys since early 1970s, no landing, Galileo 1989 bulk data, Juno 320 km 2022, Juice and Clipper dates per [18-23].
